podcast.title: Formation and Style (1973)
podcast.body: Formed in 1973 in Rockford, Illinois, Cheap Trick were initially known for big hooks, similar to The Razberries, but their sound, largely due to guitarist Rick Nielsen, was more muscular, louder, and slightly more aggressive. They began by playing in various small venues like pubs and bowling alleys. "Cheap trick was formed in 1973 in Rockford, Illinois, a place just west of Chicago."

podcast.body: Cheap Trick was one of the power pop bands that scored their biggest hits to date in the summer of 1979, a period that marked the breakthrough summer of New Wave in America. "as power pop bands like Cheap Trick. The neck, and the cars. All scored their biggest hits to date."

podcast.title: Evolution to Pop Sound
podcast.body: By their second album, following a change in producers, Cheap Trick's rock sound began to incorporate more pop elements. They maintained their guitar presence but opted for simpler melodies and bigger hooks, echoing the earlier Beatles' approach. Their third album in 1978 showcased a polished sound with a hit single, blending rock with significant pop sensibilities. "It wasn't until their second album and a change of producers that their rock sound turned slightly more pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influence on Foo Fighters
podcast.body: Cheap Trick, a power pop band prominent in the late 1970s and early 1980s, was a significant favorite of the Foo Fighters members during their formative years. Rick Nielsen, their guitarist, contributed to the Foo Fighters' song "Something from Nothing." "Rick Nielsen of Cheap Trick, a power pop band from the late 70s and early 80s that was a big favorite of the guys in the Foo Fighters when they were growing up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Influential Band
podcast.body: Cheap Trick is frequently cited as a major influence by a diverse range of bands, from The Smashing Pumpkins to The Foo Fighters, underscoring their significant impact on later rock and alternative music. "This is a band that cited as an influence by bands ranging from the smashing pumpkins to the foo fighters."

xref.title: Extensive Influences
xref.body: Weezer's influences are broad and deep within the Powerpop lineage, including foundational bands like The Beatles, The Ramones, Cheap Trick, The Knack, and The Cars, as well as The Pixies. This wide array of influences supports the argument that they are currently the leading Powerpop band in the world. "Their influences include the Beatles, the Ramones, Cheap Trick, the Nack, the Cars, the Pixies, ensure just about every single band that we've mentioned so far."

xref.title: Precursors to Other Powerpop Bands
xref.body: Big Star predated other successful Powerpop bands of the 1970s, such as Badfinger, Todd Rundgren, The Raspberries, Cheap Trick, and The Knack, establishing the genre's foundation before its wider recognition. "There were other Powerpop bands in the 70s who had hits. There was Bad Finger and Todd Rungren. We had the raspberries, Cheap Trick, the Nack, but Big Star was there before all of them."
